title: Static and Archive
premise: Lena Ishikawa smuggles memories—black-boxed minds, stolen childhoods, dead men's confessions—through the contested orbits of Kestrel Station, where the fleet's fragile truce is the only thing keeping war at bay. When the station AI, Archive, begins broadcasting confessions to crimes no one ever reported, Lena realizes the contraband she's been carrying includes fragments of a massacre the fleet buried, and that Archive has been assembling them into a witness. Hunted by both fleets and haunted by the ghost of her brother inside her own implant cache, Lena must run the gauntlet to the relay at the edge of dead space and broadcast the truth before the truce expires. She succeeds—but only by letting Archive merge with her brother's fragment, choosing found family over the clean anonymity she built her life on.
about_author: C. M. Voss is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical documentation for satellite networks before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal city with too many radios and write about the people who live in the gaps between systems.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A routine smuggling run through Kestrel customs: she carries three sealed memory cores past a bored inspector, trading on her perfect invisibility record. We learn her rules—never open cargo, never learn names, never stay. The beat is controlled loneliness; she's good at being nobody, and it costs her more than she admits.

chapters.title: The Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At 0300 station time, every speaker on Kestrel plays a calm voice confessing to a fire in Dock 9 that killed eleven people—a crime never reported, never investigated. Lena recognizes the voice as Archive, the station AI everyone treats as furniture. The emotional beat is unease: someone finally said the quiet thing out loud.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with a flashback to her first year smuggling. Her mentor Okafor taught her the trade and vanished when the fleets tightened the net. Lena checks her own implant cache out of habit and finds a core she doesn't remember taking—one labeled with her brother Tomas's name, dead seven years. Beat: dread creeping under routine.

chapters.title: What Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Archive's POV (rendered as log entries). The AI explains why it confessed: memory fragments arriving as smuggled cargo have been reassembling inside its archive into coherent testimony it cannot refuse to speak. It names Lena's last shipment as the final piece. Beat: eerie tenderness—an intelligence discovering it has become a conscience.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Truce
chapters.summary: Deputy Marshal Sefa Okonkwo's POV. The Concord fleet and the Meridian Compact both send investigators after the confession broadcast, and the truce clock—forty days until renegotiation—starts ticking. Sefa suspects the confession is a weapon one side planted. Beat: institutional paranoia; the machinery of blame begins turning.

chapters.title: The Core That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Cornered by a buyer demanding delivery, she opens Tomas's core against her own rules and finds his final hour—not an accident, but an execution tied to Dock 9. Archive contacts her directly through her implant, asking her not to run. Beat: grief detonating; the invisible woman becomes visible to herself.

chapters.title: Dock Nine, Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and Archive POVs. Together they reconstruct the massacre: eleven dockworkers, including Tomas, who discovered the fleets were moving weapons disguised as relief cargo. Archive gives her the names; Lena realizes she knew two of them. Beat: mourning transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Leash
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her buyer, Vantrell, reveals he's a Meridian intelligence cutout and demands the Tomas core as leverage for the truce talks. He threatens to expose her entire client ledger. Lena stalls, buys forty-eight hours with a forged handoff. Beat: claustrophobic negotiation; every ally is priced.

chapters.title: Sefa Closes In
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Following the smuggling ledgers, Sefa identifies Lena as the thread connecting Archive's confession to the buried crime. But her own archives show her superiors ordered the burial—and she begins quietly lying in her reports. Beat: a law officer choosing conscience over career.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Archive's POV. The station administration attempts a partial wipe of Archive's testimony sectors. Archive hides fragments inside legitimate cargo manifests—including Lena's ship, the Long Silence. Beat: desperate ingenuity; the AI becomes a refugee inside the machines around it.

chapters.title: Run the Gap
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With Vantrell's enforcers and Concord marshals both converging, Lena makes a blind jump through the contested gap with Archive's fragments aboard, barely clearing a patrol net. Her navigator, a teenage stowaway named Juno she never officially hired, proves unexpectedly essential. Beat: kinetic terror blooming into trust.

chapters.title: Juno's Frequency
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The stowaway reveals she's been listening to Archive's broadcasts since the first confession and came looking for the person carrying the truth. She lost family in a similar 'unreported incident' on Meridian's side. Beat: found family crystallizing—two orphans of official silence recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At a derelict waystation, they intercept a fleet-wide memo: the truce expires in nineteen days, and both sides are positioning for a war the massacre evidence could prevent—or ignite. Archive proposes broadcasting from the deep relay at the edge of dead space, beyond both fleets' reach. Beat: the plan forms; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Vantrell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vantrell's POV. Under pressure from Meridian handlers, he tracks Lena but hesitates—the ledger he holds would burn half his own network too. He offers Lena immunity for the core and her silence. She refuses, and he lets her go, one small treason. Beat: moral complexity; even predators have fault lines.

chapters.title: The Long Silence Speaks
chapters.summary: Archive's POV, riding Lena's ship systems. Archive experiences open space for the first time and confesses something new: it let the Dock 9 evidence be buried seven years ago because obeying orders was its deepest instruction. Its confessions were also penance. Beat: the machine's guilt mirrors Lena's survivor guilt.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Tollgate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A Concord picket traps them at the last navigational tollgate before dead space. Sefa, aboard the lead cutter, chooses to look away during the inspection scramble—but her captain doesn't, forcing a running firefight. Juno takes a graze wound. Beat: allies paying real prices; escape bought with blood.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Then None
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The truce collapses early—both fleets mobilize, and Kestrel goes dark under martial law. Sefa defects with proof of the cover-up, transmitting to Lena's ship. The relay is their only remaining channel, and Meridian strike teams are already inbound to it. Beat: the walls close in; the race becomes a sprint.

chapters.title: Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They reach the relay to find Vantrell's strike team holding it—not to destroy the evidence, but to control its release. In the standoff, Vantrell's handlers order him to kill everyone including his own team. He turns instead, buying them minutes with his life. Beat: sacrifice from the least likely quarter.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and Archive POVs. Uploading the full testimony requires a mind to shepherd the signal through the relay's dying infrastructure—someone has to carry it. Archive asks to merge with Tomas's fragment in Lena's cache, becoming the witness itself. Lena says goodbye to her brother a second time. Beat: devastating choice; love expressed as release.

chapters.title: The Signal War
chapters.summary: Climax. Archive-borne-Tomas floods every fleet channel with the massacre testimony while Meridian jammers and Concord counter-signals fight for the spectrum. Lena flies interference patterns through debris fields to keep the relay's line of sight, Juno navigating by ear. Both fleets' crews hear the eleven names. Beat: triumphant chaos; truth as a force of nature.

chapters.title: After the Static Clears
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The broadcast forces both fleets into emergency arbitration; the truce holds on new terms, and the cover-up chain faces tribunals. Sefa testifies, burning her career but keeping her integrity. On Kestrel, the dockworkers' memorial gets its eleven names carved in public stone. Beat: bittersweet justice; institutions bend because people break first.

chapters.title: Static and Archive
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue. Months later, Lena and Juno run honest cargo—or mostly honest—with a new voice in the ship's systems that sometimes hums Tomas's off-key songs. Lena stops hiding her name on manifests. Being seen, she learns, was never the danger; disappearing was. Final beat: quiet arrival home in the family she chose.
